subject: How Does Bayesian Disease Mapping/INLA Handle Missing Areal Data?

messages.author: 1c29719a737f20c6
messages.subject: How Does Bayesian Disease Mapping/INLA Handle Missing Areal Data?
parts:
Hi, all-

Bayesian disease mapping using INLA seems to be a great alternative to the frequentist approach to Small Area Estimation (SAE)--viz., multi-level modelling. Still, one weakness seems to be that INLA doesn't produce estimates (as far as I know) for areal units that don't have outcome data. Multi-level modelling would produce estimates for a geographical unit on which there is no information (say, a multi-stage sample survey that didn't include residents of a given ZIP Code) by using the parameters of the global, fixed effects--that is, the "synthetic estimate"--to produce an ZIP Code-level estimate of the quantity of interest.  The intuition is that the geographical unit with no information on outcomes is similar to other units that do have information.  

What's the analogous Bayesian disease mapping approach?  And, how is it implemented in R-INLA?  

Thanks,
David

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How Does Bayesian Disease Mapping/INLA Handle Missing Areal Data?
parts:
You just add where you want to predict in your model and set the data there to NA.  And set control.predictor=list(compute=T)
